findings.title: The canonical top-level requiredNowUnchanged field states 26 against a live required-now of 28 — two adopted acts stale — and the artifact simultaneously states 28 in three other places, so what it asserts about required-now is both false and self-contradictory
findings.where: requiredNowUnchanged (top level), and the doesNot entry 'Does not change required-now 26.'

measured.liveValue: The live file 08 condition-4 cell reads '28 of 28 required gates name a recorded identifier', and the live gate table carries 32 DR-G rows. Required-now is 28.
measured.howStale: 26 was the correct value at HEAD 5d5d778, before D-167 took it to 27 and D-169 took it to 28. Frozen v8 carries requiredNowUnchanged 26 at head 5d5d778, where it was true. v9 carried the number forward across two adopted acts.
measured.internalContradiction: The same artifact asserts 28 three times: authorityClaim 'It does not change live required-now 28', summary.requiredNowUnchanged 28, and doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone 'Live required-now stays 28.' So the file states both 26 and 28.
measured.whatWasRefreshed: head, file08Pin, all 62 basedOn pins, all 61 recordedInputs digests and summary.requiredNowUnchanged were all updated to post-D-169 values. The top-level cardinality and one doesNot line were not.

findings.whyBlockerNotShouldFix: Both of my severity tests are met, not one. It is false against the live register — required-now is 28, not 26 — on the exact field the dispatch names and the attack list targets. And because the artifact asserts 26 and 28 in the same document, what it claims about required-now is undecidable from the artifact alone; a reader cannot tell which value it means. Materiality follows from what the field is for: requiredNowUnchanged is the canonical top-level cardinality that successors pin and quote throughout this corpus, and summary is a summary. A downstream artifact reading the top-level field gets a condition-4 fact that is two adopted acts wrong. It is also stale in precisely the dimension this version exists to refresh: v9's stated purpose is to remeasure after D-169, and D-169's own adopted text instructed 'Do not copy stale snapshot arithmetic if file 08 has moved.' Everything else was remeasured; the cardinality was copied.
findings.whatIsNotWrong: The substance of the remeasurement is correct and is not affected. OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION correctly flips to leftoverDesign false at existingGate DR-G32 with rideStanding qualification-at-named-gate and owner 'Operability + security', which matches the live DR-G32 owner cell. All seven still-open remainders stay true. Every digest recomputes. This is a single stale number in two places, not a structural defect.
findings.fix: Set the top-level requiredNowUnchanged to 28, matching summary.requiredNowUnchanged and the live condition-4 cell, and change the doesNot entry to 'Does not change required-now 28.' No obligation, flag or bucket needs to move.

observationsNotFindings: The blocker is a single number in two places, and it sits inside an artifact that is otherwise the most thoroughly remeasured in this sweep: 62 basedOn pins and 61 recordedInputs digests all recompute, head and file08Pin both carry post-D-169 values, and summary.requiredNowUnchanged was correctly updated to 28. That is what makes the omission worth a blocker rather than a shrug — the author demonstrably re-measured everything else, so the stale 26 is not a version written before the world moved but a field that was skipped while its own summary counterpart was fixed.

The substantive transition is handled well. Moving OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION from leftover-design to qualification-at-named-gate is exactly what D-169 licenses, and the reason names the surviving remainder — G32 execution once fixtures exist — rather than treating the naming as if it had discharged the obligation. The seven authoring and BLK remainders are untouched. A weaker document would have let the gate becoming live soften the neighbouring flags.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One blocker, no should-fix. The top-level requiredNowUnchanged reads 26. Live required-now is 28 — the condition-4 cell reads '28 of 28 required gates name a recorded identifier' and the gate table carries 32 rows. 26 was correct at HEAD 5d5d778, before D-167 took it to 27 and D-169 took it to 28, and frozen v8 carries 26 at that head; v9 carried the number across two adopted acts. A doesNot entry repeats it as 'Does not change required-now 26.' The same file states 28 three times — authorityClaim, summary.requiredNowUnchanged, and doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone — so the artifact is not merely stale but self-contradictory, and what it asserts about required-now cannot be determined from it. I graded it a blocker because it is false against the live register on the field the dispatch names, because requiredNowUnchanged is the canonical top-level cardinality successors pin and quote while summary is a summary, and because v9's whole purpose is remeasurement after D-169, whose own adopted text says 'Do not copy stale snapshot arithmetic if file 08 has moved.' What makes it a slip rather than a wholesale failure is that everything else was refreshed: all 62 basedOn pins and 61 recordedInputs recompute, head and file08Pin carry post-D-169 values, and summary.requiredNowUnchanged was itself corrected to 28. The fix is to set the top-level field to 28 and amend the one doesNot line; no obligation, flag or bucket moves. Everything substantive is right: OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION correctly flips to leftoverDesign false at existingGate DR-G32 with owner matching the live DR-G32 cell, all seven authoring and BLK remainders stay true, thirty obligations bucket cleanly with no misbucket, both liveGateOwners entries match live cells by ==, and gates 2 and 3 are stated not to hold with DR-114 staying OPEN. 16 attacks run, 15 refuted, one landing.
